roles.enD: Nothing assumed. Safe places to practise and the references worth reading first.
roles.arD: لا يفترض شيئا مسبقا، وهي أماكن آمنة للتدرب والمراجع الجديرة بالقراءة أولا.

roles.enD: Binary exploitation, reversing, web, crypto, forensics and stego.
roles.arD: استغلال الثنائيات والهندسة العكسية والويب والتعمية والأدلة الرقمية والإخفاء.

roles.enD: Reconnaissance, scanning, exploitation and post exploitation.
roles.arD: الاستطلاع والمسح والاستغلال وما بعد الاستغلال.

roles.enD: Detection engineering, monitoring, incident response and forensics.
roles.arD: هندسة الكشف والمراقبة والاستجابة للحوادث والتحليل الجنائي.

roles.enD: Finding flaws in code, dependencies and running applications.
roles.arD: اكتشاف العلل في الشيفرة والاعتماديات والتطبيقات العاملة.

roles.enD: Posture, policy and runtime security for cloud and Kubernetes.
roles.arD: الوضع الأمني والسياسات وأمن التشغيل للسحابة وكوبرنيتس.

roles.enD: Frameworks, hardening baselines and evidence you can hand to an auditor.
roles.arD: الأطر وخطوط التحصين والأدلة التي تقدم للمدقق.

roles.enD: Collecting, storing and sharing what is known about threats.
roles.arD: جمع ما هو معلوم عن التهديدات وحفظه ومشاركته.

roles.enD: Analysing samples safely and building on the work of others.
roles.arD: تحليل العينات بأمان والبناء على عمل الآخرين.

tools.name: the-book-of-secret-knowledge
tools.note: A wide index of tools and one-liners. Useful for finding out what exists.
tools.description: A collection of inspiring lists, manuals, cheatsheets, blogs, hacks, one-liners, cli/web tools and more.

tools.name: sherlock
tools.note: Finds a username across social networks.
tools.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks

tools.name: PayloadsAllTheThings
tools.note: Payloads and bypasses per vulnerability class. The reference you will keep open.
tools.description: A list of useful payloads and bypass for Web Application Security and Pentest/CTF

tools.name: ghidra
tools.note: A full reverse engineering suite with a decompiler, free and open. The default starting point.
tools.description: Ghidra is a software reverse engineering (SRE) framework

tools.name: SecLists
tools.note: Wordlists for usernames, passwords, directories and payloads. Almost every tool wants one.
tools.description: SecLists is the security tester's companion. It's a collection of multiple types of lists used during security assessments, collected in one place. List types include usernames, passwords, URLs, sensitive data patterns, fuzzing payloads, web shells, and many more.

tools.name: metasploit-framework
tools.note: The exploitation framework. Worth learning for the workflow as much as the exploits.
tools.description: Metasploit Framework

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.note: Automated SQL injection detection and exploitation. Understand the injection first.
tools.description: Automatic SQL injection and database takeover tool

tools.name: trivy
tools.note: Scans images, filesystems and repositories for vulnerabilities and misconfiguration.
tools.description: Find vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, secrets, SBOM in containers, Kubernetes, code repositories, clouds and more

tools.name: nuclei
tools.note: Template driven vulnerability scanning. The template library is the real product.
tools.description: Nuclei is a fast, customizable vulnerability scanner powered by the global security community and built on a simple YAML-based DSL, enabling collaboration to tackle trending vulnerabilities on the internet. It helps you find vulnerabilities in your applications, APIs, networks, DNS, and cloud configurations.

tools.name: gitleaks
tools.note: Finds secrets in git history, not just the working tree.
tools.description: Find secrets with Gitleaks 🔑

tools.name: trufflehog
tools.note: Secret scanning that verifies whether a found credential is actually live.
tools.description: Find, verify, and analyze leaked credentials

tools.name: hashcat
tools.note: GPU password recovery. Fast, and the rule engine repays study.
tools.description: World's fastest and most advanced password recovery utility

tools.name: radare2
tools.note: Command line reverse engineering framework. Steep, fast, scriptable.
tools.description: UNIX-like reverse engineering framework and command-line toolset

tools.name: spiderfoot
tools.note: Automates OSINT collection across a large number of modules.
tools.description: SpiderFoot automates OSINT for threat intelligence and mapping your attack surface.

tools.name: vulhub
tools.note: Pre-built vulnerable environments in Docker, one per CVE. Reproduce a real bug in a minute.
tools.description: Pre-Built Vulnerable Environments Based on Docker-Compose

tools.name: cutter
tools.note: A graphical front end for rizin, for when the command line is in the way.
tools.description: Free and Open Source Reverse Engineering Platform powered by rizin

tools.name: theHarvester
tools.note: Collects emails, subdomains and hosts from public sources. An early recon step.
tools.description: E-mails, subdomains and names Harvester - OSINT

tools.name: wazuh
tools.note: Open host monitoring with file integrity, log analysis and compliance checks.
tools.description: Wazuh - The Open Source Security Platform. Unified XDR and SIEM protection for endpoints and cloud workloads.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.note: Fast web fuzzing for directories, parameters and virtual hosts.
tools.description: Fast web fuzzer written in Go

tools.name: semgrep
tools.note: Static analysis where rules look like the code they match. Easy to write your own.
tools.description: Lightweight static analysis for many languages. Find bug variants with patterns that look like source code.

tools.name: lynis
tools.note: Host hardening audit for Unix systems. Produces findings you can act on the same day.
tools.description: Lynis - Security auditing tool for Linux, macOS, and UNIX-based systems. Assists with compliance testing (HIPAA/ISO27001/PCI DSS) and system hardening. Agentless, and installation optional.

tools.name: impacket
tools.note: Python implementations of network protocols. The backbone of most Windows attack tooling.
tools.description: Impacket is a collection of Python classes for working with network protocols.

tools.name: zaproxy
tools.note: An intercepting proxy and scanner. The open alternative for learning web testing.
tools.description: The ZAP by Checkmarx Core project

tools.name: XSStrike
tools.note: Cross site scripting detection that checks context rather than firing payloads blindly.
tools.description: Most advanced XSS scanner.

tools.name: amass
tools.note: In depth attack surface mapping and external asset discovery.
tools.description: In-depth attack surface mapping and asset discovery

tools.name: prowler
tools.note: Security assessment across AWS, Azure and GCP with compliance frameworks built in.
tools.description: Prowler is the world’s most widely used open-source cloud security platform that automates security and compliance across any cloud environment.

tools.name: dirsearch
tools.note: Web path discovery with sensible defaults for someone starting out.
tools.description: Web path scanner

tools.name: subfinder
tools.note: Passive subdomain discovery across many sources.
tools.description: Fast passive subdomain enumeration tool.

tools.name: gobuster
tools.note: Directory, DNS and virtual host brute forcing. Simple and quick.
tools.description: Directory/File, DNS and VHost busting tool written in Go

tools.name: juice-shop
tools.note: A deliberately broken web shop covering the whole OWASP Top 10. The usual first target.
tools.description: OWASP Juice Shop: Probably the most modern and sophisticated insecure web application

tools.name: pwntools
tools.note: The exploit development library. Turns a page of socket handling into three lines.
tools.description: CTF framework and exploit development library

tools.name: DVWA
tools.note: Damn Vulnerable Web Application. Small, old, and still the clearest way to see a SQL injection work.
tools.description: Damn Vulnerable Web Application (DVWA)

tools.name: john
tools.note: John the Ripper. Handles more formats than anything else.
tools.description: John the Ripper jumbo - advanced offline password cracker, which supports hundreds of hash and cipher types, and runs on many operating systems, CPUs, GPUs, and even some FPGAs

tools.name: nmap
tools.note: Port and service discovery, plus a scripting engine most people never touch. Learn it properly.
tools.description: Nmap - the Network Mapper. Github mirror of official SVN repository.

tools.name: grype
tools.note: Vulnerability scanning for container images and filesystems.
tools.description: A vulnerability scanner for container images and filesystems

tools.name: oss-fuzz
tools.note: Continuous fuzzing for open source projects, and a good model to copy.
tools.description: OSS-Fuzz - continuous fuzzing for open source software.

tools.name: atomic-red-team
tools.note: Small tests mapped to ATT&CK, so you can check whether your detections actually fire.
tools.description: Small and highly portable detection tests based on MITRE's ATT&CK.

tools.name: opa
tools.note: General policy engine. Write the rule once and enforce it anywhere.
tools.description: Open Policy Agent (OPA) is an open source, general-purpose policy engine.

tools.name: Detect-It-Easy
tools.note: Identifies packers, compilers and protectors. The first thing to run on an unknown file.
tools.description: Program for determining types of files for Windows, Linux and MacOS.

tools.name: sigma
tools.note: A vendor neutral format for detection rules, plus a large rule library. Write once, convert.
tools.description: Main Sigma Rule Repository

tools.name: pwndbg
tools.note: The other gdb enhancement. Try both and keep whichever you read faster.
tools.description: Exploit Development and Reverse Engineering with GDB & LLDB Made Easy

tools.name: httpx
tools.note: Probes a list of hosts and tells you what is actually serving HTTP.
tools.description: httpx is a fast and multi-purpose HTTP toolkit that allows running multiple probes using the retryablehttp library.

tools.name: opencti
tools.note: Knowledge graph for threat intelligence, structured around STIX.
tools.description: Open Cyber Threat Intelligence Platform

tools.name: yara
tools.note: Pattern matching for files. How malware families are described and identified.
tools.description: The pattern matching swiss knife

tools.name: wireshark
tools.note: Packet analysis. The tool you reach for when the answer is in the traffic.
tools.description: Read-only mirror of Wireshark's Git repository at https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark. You're welcome to submit pull requests there.

tools.name: wstg
tools.note: The Web Security Testing Guide. What to test and how, rather than which tool to run.
tools.description: The Web Security Testing Guide is a comprehensive Open Source guide to testing the security of web applications and web services.

tools.name: syft
tools.note: Generates a software bill of materials. Increasingly something you are asked to produce.
tools.description: CLI tool and library for generating a Software Bill of Materials from container images and filesystems

tools.name: falco
tools.note: Runtime detection for containers based on kernel events.
tools.description: Cloud Native Runtime Security

tools.name: angr
tools.note: Symbolic execution. Solves reversing challenges by asking what input reaches the win branch.
tools.description: A powerful and user-friendly binary analysis platform!

tools.name: flare-vm
tools.note: Turns a Windows VM into a malware analysis workstation with one script.
tools.description: A collection of software installations scripts for Windows systems that allows you to easily setup and maintain a reverse engineering environment on a VM.

tools.name: checkov
tools.note: Policy as code for Terraform, CloudFormation and Kubernetes manifests.
tools.description: Prevent cloud misconfigurations and find vulnerabilities during build-time in infrastructure as code, container images and open source packages with Checkov by Bridgecrew.

tools.name: gef
tools.note: Adds heap inspection, memory maps and pattern search to gdb. Written for exploitation.
tools.description: GEF (GDB Enhanced Features) - a modern experience for GDB with advanced debugging capabilities for exploit devs & reverse engineers on Linux

tools.name: bandit
tools.note: Finds common security problems in Python. Small and quick to adopt.
tools.description: Bandit is a tool designed to find common security issues in Python code.

tools.name: kube-bench
tools.note: Checks a Kubernetes cluster against the CIS benchmark.
tools.description: Checks whether Kubernetes is deployed according to security best practices as defined in the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark

tools.name: zeek
tools.note: Turns traffic into structured logs rather than alerts. Different question, better answers.
tools.description: Zeek is a powerful network analysis framework that is much different from the typical IDS you may know.

tools.name: ScoutSuite
tools.note: Multi cloud auditing that produces a readable report rather than raw findings.
tools.description: Multi-Cloud Security Auditing Tool

tools.name: DependencyCheck
tools.note: Maps your dependencies to known vulnerabilities. Long established.
tools.description: OWASP dependency-check is a software composition analysis utility that detects publicly disclosed vulnerabilities in application dependencies.

tools.name: aircrack-ng
tools.note: Wireless auditing. Still the reference for testing your own network.
tools.description: WiFi security auditing tools suite

tools.name: RsaCtfTool
tools.note: Tries every known attack against a weak RSA key. Solves most competition crypto.
tools.description: RSA attack tool (mainly for ctf) - retrieve private key from weak public key and/or uncipher data

tools.name: AFLplusplus
tools.note: The maintained fork of AFL. Where fuzzing usually starts.
tools.description: The fuzzer afl++ is afl with community patches, qemu 5.1 upgrade, collision-free coverage, enhanced laf-intel & redqueen, AFLfast++ power schedules, MOpt mutators, unicorn_mode, and a lot more!

tools.name: suricata
tools.note: Network intrusion detection and traffic logging.
tools.description: Suricata is a network Intrusion Detection System, Intrusion Prevention System and Network Security Monitoring engine developed by the OISF and the Suricata community.

tools.name: MISP
tools.note: The threat intelligence sharing platform most communities standardised on.
tools.description: MISP (core software) - Open Source Threat Intelligence and Sharing Platform

tools.name: slither
tools.note: Static analysis for Solidity, if your target is a smart contract.
tools.description: Static Analyzer for Solidity and Vyper

tools.name: naabu
tools.note: Fast port scanning designed to feed the rest of the pipeline.
tools.description: A fast port scanner written in go with a focus on reliability and simplicity. Designed to be used in combination with other tools for attack surface discovery in bug bounties and pentests

tools.name: capa
tools.note: Describes what a binary does in terms of capabilities rather than bytes.
tools.description: The FLARE team's open-source tool to identify capabilities in executable files.

tools.name: NetExec
tools.note: Network execution across SMB, WinRM and more. The successor to CrackMapExec.
tools.description: The Network Execution Tool

tools.name: metasploitable3
tools.note: A whole vulnerable machine rather than one app, for practising the full path in.
tools.description: Metasploitable3 is a VM that is built from the ground up with a large amount of security vulnerabilities.

tools.name: ansible-collection-hardening
tools.note: Hardening roles you can apply rather than a checklist you have to implement.
tools.description: This Ansible collection provides battle tested hardening for Linux, SSH, nginx, MySQL

tools.name: Empire
tools.note: Post exploitation and command framework, useful for understanding how implants work.
tools.description: Empire is a post-exploitation and adversary emulation framework that is used to aid Red Teams and Penetration Testers.

tools.name: terrascan
tools.note: Detects compliance and security violations in infrastructure as code.
tools.description: Detect compliance and security violations across Infrastructure as Code to mitigate risk before provisioning cloud native infrastructure.

tools.name: grr
tools.note: Remote live forensics across a fleet, from Google.
tools.description: GRR Rapid Response: remote live forensics for incident response

tools.name: kube-hunter
tools.note: Hunts for weaknesses in a Kubernetes cluster from inside or outside.
tools.description: Hunt for security weaknesses in Kubernetes clusters

tools.name: securityonion
tools.note: A whole monitoring distribution. The fastest way to a working lab SOC.
tools.description: Security Onion is a free and open platform for threat hunting, enterprise security monitoring, and log management. It includes our own interfaces for alerting, dashboards, hunting, PCAP, detections, and case management. It also includes other tools such as osquery, CyberChef, Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana, Suricata, and Zeek.

tools.name: detect-secrets
tools.note: Built to keep new secrets out rather than to find old ones.
tools.description: An enterprise friendly way of detecting and preventing secrets in code.

tools.name: ROPgadget
tools.note: Finds gadgets in a binary so you can build a return oriented chain.
tools.description: This tool lets you search your gadgets on your binaries to facilitate your ROP exploitation. ROPgadget supports ELF, PE and Mach-O format on x86, x64, ARM, ARM64, PowerPC, SPARC, MIPS, RISC-V 64, and RISC-V Compressed architectures.

tools.name: volatility3
tools.note: Memory forensics. Pulls processes, connections and injected code from a memory image.
tools.description: Volatility 3.0 development

tools.name: velociraptor
tools.note: Endpoint visibility and hunting at scale, with its own query language.
tools.description: Digging Deeper....

tools.name: TheHive
tools.note: Case management for incident response. This is the last open version, kept because it still runs.
tools.description: TheHive is a Collaborative Case Management Platform, now distributed as a commercial version

tools.name: chainsaw
tools.note: Hunts through Windows event logs with Sigma rules. Pairs well with hayabusa.
tools.description: Rapidly Search and Hunt through Windows Forensic Artefacts

tools.name: CAPEv2
tools.note: Sandbox built for extracting configuration and unpacking payloads.
tools.description: Malware Configuration And Payload Extraction

tools.name: BloodHound
tools.note: Maps Active Directory as a graph and finds the path to domain admin.
tools.description: Six Degrees of Domain Admin

tools.name: hayabusa
tools.note: Fast Windows event log triage with a built in rule set. Answers what happened, quickly.
tools.description: Hayabusa (隼) is a sigma-based threat hunting and fast forensics timeline generator for Windows event logs.

tools.name: autopsy
tools.note: Disk forensics with a graphical interface, built on The Sleuth Kit.
tools.description: Autopsy® is a digital forensics platform and graphical interface to The Sleuth Kit® and other digital forensics tools. It can be used by law enforcement, military, and corporate examiners to investigate what happened on a computer. You can even use it to recover photos from your camera's memory card.

tools.name: content
tools.note: Hardening content and profiles for many baselines, including CIS and STIG.
tools.description: Security automation content in SCAP, Bash, Ansible, and other formats

tools.name: detection-rules
tools.note: Elastic's production detection rules, in the open. Read them for how a real rule is built.

tools.name: stego-toolkit
tools.note: A container with the stego tools already installed, so you can stop hunting for them.
tools.description: Collection of steganography tools - helps with CTF challenges

tools.name: attack-navigator
tools.note: Layers your coverage over the ATT&CK matrix. The standard way to show gaps.
tools.description: Web app that provides basic navigation and annotation of ATT&CK matrices

tools.name: plaso
tools.note: Builds a super timeline from every artefact on a disk. Slow, thorough, invaluable.
tools.description: Super timeline all the things

tools.name: Ropper
tools.note: Gadget search with a different interface and useful binary information.
tools.description: Display information about files in different file formats and find gadgets to build rop chains for different architectures (x86/x86_64, ARM/ARM64, MIPS, PowerPC, SPARC64). For disassembly ropper uses the awesome Capstone Framework.

tools.name: cti
tools.note: ATT&CK itself in STIX form, so you can build against it rather than read it.
tools.description: Cyber Threat Intelligence Repository expressed in STIX 2.0

tools.name: openscap
tools.note: The scanner that consumes SCAP content and produces audit ready reports.
tools.description: NIST Certified SCAP 1.2 toolkit

tools.name: OSCAL
tools.note: A machine readable format for control catalogues and assessment results.
tools.description: Open Security Controls Assessment Language (OSCAL)

tools.name: Kuwait-NBCC
tools.note: The Kuwait national baseline, all 44 controls with checks and evidence, bilingual.
tools.description: Understand, assess and evidence compliance with the Kuwait National Basic Cybersecurity Controls (NBCC), Annex 1 to NCSC Decision No. 2 of 2026. 44 controls, 329 checks, due 5 October 2027.

tools.name: miftah
tools.note: Cryptographic inventory and post quantum readiness, producing a CBOM.
tools.description: Cryptographic inventory and post quantum readiness. Scans code, certificates and live endpoints, writes a CycloneDX 1.6 CBOM, and scores exposure with Mosca inequality. Zero dependencies.
